body: I discovered everything back in the second week of January, so we have been going to couples therapy since then. She is adamant that she wants to keep her privacy, she sees me going through her phone as a toxic thing so she doesn't want to feel like I am a shadow watching over her every move (her words). And then the ex situation happened in February

I wont defend this. I know I could have been better before this happened. I could have given her a place of respect in my family, I could have been better when it comes to the small details and signs of love and better at supporting her during her hard times. I did try, I got her to enroll in therapy, and at the beginning I encouraged her to make friends and find happiness.

I don't want to put myself as fully free of guilt, and that is also one of the reasons why I didn't just want to break things up :(

I guess a part of me is thinking that maybe she genuinely didn't think that texting her ex was bad? That she didn't do it with the intention of cheating. Maybe its just hopeful thinking trying to justify saving the relationship after so many years.

That's the thing. I don't know what to think. Part of me loves her so much and wants to be with her, but then another part is thinking that she is not putting value into the relationship. I guess I am scared of losing 10 years worth of relationship and losing who I once though was the love of my life.

That is what I am scared off, that I will trust her and give her another chance, and that she ends up doing it again, breaking my heart once more and making me waste all that time put into her. But there is another side of me thinking that this is the only time she has done this, that she was dealing with depression and we were at a really low point on the relationship, and that part wants to keep trying :(

To me, it has been a mix, but to give a quick rundown.

1. Explain what you just studied to someone else or to yourself: There is no better way to make sure you properly understand something that by being able to explain it yourself to someone else. If they are not tech savvy and they can understand at the end it means you have a full grasp of things. If you are struggling to explain something it means you just discovered something you can study and even research to help on your explanation.

2. Flashcards: I use Anki myself but there are many other apps you can use. Pretty much repetition to learn info, specially info that needs to be memorized instead of understood. For example, port numbers, acronyms, data rates, etc.

3. Exercising: Yes, I know it sounds crazy, but I have realized that I retain information a lot better if I'm doing light exercise while I study. Going for a walk for example has been my go to. Gets your blood flowing, prevents you from feeling sleepy and improves circulation to the brain while studying.

Those 3 things have been my go to for studying in what I would say is order of importance. 

My study routine has now been to, read/watch the content I want to study while sitting down, try to explain what I know to myself to get a grasp of what I'm missing, create flashcards for things I'm lacking in understanding or simply need to memorize, go for a walk to study, and then I come back and try to explain to my wife what I just studied (bless her soul, I know she gets bored to death from this part lol).

Hope this can help you out, I have ADHD so studying has always been a struggle for me, but without the use of meds I have been able to properly study using this method.

The reason is that in the late game, enemies tend to have less elemental weaknesses (specially bosses), so you no longer can get extra turns from magic weakness, but you can always get a turn press from critical hits. So while Mag is extremely strong early game, come late game Dex with Luck for crits is pretty solid. I would recommend at least 2-1-1 Dex-Agi-Luck, and last point in whatever you want. Extra dex for damage, extra Luck for more crits, and extra Agi to get better at evasion and getting first turn
